title: What Cyber Security Actually Is, and How You Get Into It
location: 42 Wakefield Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010, Auckland
description:
# **Nyuk Loong Kiw**

**Group Chief Information Security Officer, Spark New Zealand**
Nyuk Loong Kiw is the Group Chief Information Security Officer at Spark New Zealand, leading the organisation's cyber security strategy and operations. His career spans more than two decades at Spark, progressing from desktop support through network engineering, security engineering, incident response, and Security Operations Centre leadership before becoming CISO.
Drawing on extensive real-world experience, Nyuk Loong brings practical insights into how modern cyber security functions within a large enterprise, combining technical expertise, business strategy, risk management, and organisational resilience.

***

# Topic

Cyber security is often misunderstood as a highly technical field limited to hackers and complex technology. In reality, it is a multidisciplinary profession focused on protecting organisations through people, processes, and technology.
In this session, Nyuk Loong Kiw will explain what cyber security actually looks like inside one of New Zealand's largest organisations. The first half of the presentation introduces the core responsibilities of security teams, why even well-resourced organisations experience security incidents, and the major threats affecting businesses today, including phishing, ransomware, weak credentials, malware, and denial-of-service attacks. Real-world examples, including local New Zealand cases, will be shared throughout the talk.
The second half focuses on careers in cyber security. As the industry shifts from simply preventing attacks to building organisational resilience, new career opportunities are emerging in areas such as detection engineering, identity architecture, AI security, and business-focused risk management. title: Agentic AI in Healthcare [in person]
description:
This month we are going to have an in person meeting about AI in Healthcare. BI and Fabric, and also a review of the most important updates recently on the Power BI and Microsoft Fabric, and the AI-related topics about it. Join us for this session of learning and networking.
**Agenda:**
5:00-5:30 PM Welcome and Networking/Refreshments
5:30-6:30 PM AI in Healthcare
6:30-7:00 PM Wrap Up
**Topic 1:** **Agentic AI in Healthcare: The RAG-Powered Diagnostic Assistant**
\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*
Parametric LLM memory cannot support clinical deployment: no provenance, no patient-specific grounding at inference time, and unacceptable hallucination rates. Retrieval-Augmented Generation solves this by grounding an agentic system's reasoning loop in dynamically retrieved, evidence-backed context instead of static model weights.

**The architecture:** Chunking and embedding heterogeneous clinical data (imaging reports, discharge summaries, structured EHR fields), dense vector indexing with approximate nearest-neighbour retrieval, and context injection into the perceive-reason-act-learn cycle.

**Key trade-offs:** Retrieval latency versus context window budget, chunk size versus semantic coherence, embedding model selection for domain terminology, and multi-agent coordination for ranking and routing evidence across specialist sub-agents.

**Results:** 94.1% diagnostic accuracy in liver cancer detection; door-to-balloon time reduced from 211 to 68 minutes in a real cardiac workflow via concurrent retrieval across imaging, history, and evidence.

**Open problems**: Explainability at the retrieval-to-reasoning boundary, bias propagation through retrieved context, and the validation gap between proof-of-concept and clinical-grade reliability.

title: In this Corner of the World (Japan, 2016)
description:
This film is a little unusual for us in the International Film Festival Meetup. However, it is appropriate for today, as a commemoration of the bombing of Hiroshima. It is also a classic example Japanese anime. So today we immerse ourselves in the Japanese experience of suffering a nuclear attack, The film won Best Film Award at the LA Film Festival in 2017.

In This Corner of the World tells the story of Suzu, a spirited 18-year-old woman is married off to a man she barely knows. She moves to the small town of Kure, the port of Hiroshima to live with her husband’s family. Suzu’s life is thrown into chaos when her town is bombed during World War II.

Her perseverance and courage, however, underpin this heart-warming and inspirational tale of the everyday challenges faced by the Japanese in the midst of a violent, war-torn country.
The film focuses on the everyday aspects of Suzu’s life, and as the war increasingly intrudes into her world, Suzu uses her artistic talents to provide herself (and the audience) with moments of fantasy and escape from those harsh realities.

In This Corner of the World film reminds us of the horrors of this day, the resilience and courage of the survivors and the reasons why it must never happen again. A Must see for those concerned for peace.

title: Beyond the Hype:
description:
Why Most Businesses Are Failing at AI, and Why Project Managers Hold the Answer

Next month **The Project Community Auckland** brings you two speakers who are helping organisations Turn AI ambition into practical, governed delivery.

**Beyond the Hype: Why Most Businesses Are Failing at AI, and Why Project Managers Hold the Answer - Delivered by Mark Lucas**

Everyone's talking about AI. Almost every business is trying to adopt it. Most are failing, and not because of the technology. Mark Lucas works at the coalface of AI adoption with New Zealand businesses, and the pattern is clear: this is a capability and change problem, not a technology one. In this session Mark cuts through the hype with real stories from the market, unpacks the link between individual and organisational AI maturity (why a business can only move as fast as its people can), and lays out the order that actually works. His argument for this room: project management discipline isn't a casualty of AI, it's the difference between the businesses pulling ahead and the ones stuck at the starting gate. With one catch: those skills only pay off when they're pointed at the right target.

**Followed by:**

**Governing AI You Can Prove — Introducing the GAICC Framework, Maturity Model, Roadmap & Credentials - Delivered by Faiz Rasool**

A free, open, standards-based operating system for turning AI ambition into governed, value-realising delivery.

AI ambition is everywhere; a coherent way to govern and deliver it is not. This session introduces the GAICC AI Governance Framework — a free, open, standards-based system that gives any organisation one navigable model for governing AI end to end.

title: A Manifesto for the AI journey
description:
How do you go from AI proof of concepts in your organisation to embedding AI in your operating model without creating chaos or ending up in a dark place? Rebecca and Duncan will give an overview of ezyVet’s AI implementation journey, and then Anthony will introduce the [Makers Manifesto](https://makersmanifesto.org/), a set of values and principles developed globally for organisations who are on this journey.

In the first part of this talk, Rebecca Kemp and Duncan Crawford from ezyVet (part of IDEXX Software) will share how their product, engineering, and UX teams are rethinking product development in the age of AI — moving from "1,000 blossoms bloom" experimentation to a deliberate approach built on tooling, capability-building, and a shared cross-functional framework. Expect real examples of what's working, like building PRDs directly from Claude transcripts, alongside an honest look at the role ambiguity and anxiety this shift creates, and how they're leading through it with clarity and optimism.

Following this Anthony Marter will introduce the [Makers Manifesto](https://makersmanifesto.org/) \- a global collaboration created by 45 product leaders from around the world which makes a statement on what good looks like for an AI enabled product making organisation\. He’ll tell the story of how this came to be from\, wrangled from the opinions of global leaders like Martin Eriksson\, Christina Wodtke and Matt LeMay\, and how it has a uniquely Aussie and Kiwi flavour\.

This will then be followed by a mini feedback workshop where you’ll get the chance to give your thoughts on the Makers Manifesto, which will help to inform the next iteration of this.

You can join the Livestream details **from 6pm** here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NMpCI2SMnzU

Massive thanks to IDEXX for hosting and sponsoring this event.
